experiments.E: E · Up and down the ramp

instructions.A: Raise one end of the track 4 cm. Point the cart's +x arrow down the track and release it from rest.
instructions.B: Raise the track to 8 cm and repeat A. How do the graphs differ from A, and how are they the same?
instructions.C: Level track, brake on. Give the cart a brief push in the +x direction and let go.
instructions.D: Level track, brake on. Give the cart a brief push in the −x direction and let go.
instructions.E: Point the +x arrow up the ramp. From near the bottom, push the cart up; it peaks and rolls back down. Catch it.

screenSummary.playArea: A cart sits on a 1.2-metre track whose left end can be raised. Below the track, graphs show the cart's velocity and acceleration against time, together with your predictions.
screenSummary.controlArea: Choose one of the lab's five experiments, adjust the incline, brake, arrow direction and push, then release or push the cart. Draw predictions on the graphs, fill in the sign table, and play, pause or step the clock.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Choose experiment A, draw your predictions, then press Release.

screenSummary.playArea: Graphs show the velocity and acceleration of a real PASCO Smart Cart against time, together with your predictions.
screenSummary.controlArea: Connect a Smart Cart over Bluetooth, choose the experiment, then record a run. Draw predictions on the graphs and fill in the sign table.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Turn on the Smart Cart, press Connect and choose it in the browser's list.

preferences.title: Simulation
preferences.accelerationSmoothingDescription: Acceleration is found by differentiating the encoder position twice, which amplifies noise. More smoothing gives a steadier acceleration graph but rounds off sudden changes.
